Definition 5.3. If n, k ∈ N with 0 ≤ k ≤ n − 1, then a k-lattice path of length 2n is a lattice
path from (0, n) to (n, 0) consisting of n steps east by (1, 0) and n steps south by (0, −1) such that
the path does not cross the line y = n − x + k. We denote the set of all k-lattice paths of length
2n as LPn,k .

Example 1. Taking p = s = 2, m = 3, n = 7, and all seven two-dimensional subspaces of Z32 as Vi , we obtain
a (21, 3)-coloring of H(7, 4) and OA(2048, 7, 4, 5), which was undiscovered according to [19, Table 12.3] (where
k := n = 7, t := 5, index is 2048/45 = 2). The derived parameters OA(512, 6, 4, 4) are also new. The union
of 3 cosets of C gives a perfect (15, 9)-coloring of H(7, 4), which reduces the upper bound in another line of the
small-value table (Appendix).
   It is possible to construct perfect colorings from additive codes that are not indepentent sets. This possibility
needs futher investigation, and here we only show one example, whose parameters occur in Appendix.
